subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm designing a static truck model, no rigging needed, facing forward with roughly 7m length, 2.6m width, and 3m height, planning six wheels across three axles using parts, extrusions, lathes, and texture work for the construction.

I'm working out the chassis frame, cab, and hood geometry using extruded cross-section outlines for the sloped windshield and body panels, defining coordinate points to shape the profile and applying paneled paint coloring.

For the windshield, I'm positioning a thin tilted box to catch the slope between the cab and hood, calculating the rotation angle needed so its face aligns with the glass plane's normal direction.

Now I'm adding glow-colored window surfaces with SVG texture striping, side window planes mounted on the x-axis, and then building the armored cargo bed as a paneled box with ribs along the sides using loops to keep the part count manageable.

I'm fleshing out the roof turret with a base ring, box body, twin glowing-muzzle barrels, then designing front details like the ram plate, light bar, grille texture, and cannon lights, plus side skirts and arched fenders over the wheels using cylinder geometry with partial arcs.

Wheels get tire, rim, hub, lug-nut rings, neon rim torus, and tread blocks via a reusable wheel helper, totaling around 96 parts across six wheels before moving on to antennas and other exterior details.

Now I'm adding exhaust stacks, missile pods, underglow strips, a license plate with svg text, roof light bar, radar dish, and warning stripe decals, while setting up box/cylinder helper functions with rotation and axis options for building each part, plus shared glow materials and several svg textures for the grille, windshield, windows, and decals, mirroring parts left-right as I go.

Still working through chassis and wheel positions, then figuring out fender flares using slab boxes with angled front/back pieces instead of a tricky partial cylinder arc.

Placing the door decal plane on the cab side so it reads upright when viewed from outside, then nudging the windshield glass slightly outward from the cab's sloped outline to avoid z-fighting.

For the windshield itself, I'll use a textured plane oriented with its normal tilted toward +Y/+Z instead of a box, applying a cyan gradient with HUD lines and a subtle glow. Then I'm setting up the turret assembly on the cargo roof: a ring base, a boxy housing, and twin barrels extending along the z-axis.

Now I'm adding side-mounted rocket pods with grid-patterned tube openings and glowing orange warhead tips facing forward, rear tail lights and hazard-striped door details, a roof light bar with antennas and a radar dish, and a front ram bumper with glowing headlight boxes.

Still placing details... grille texture, hood vents and stripe, lower skirts, underglow boxes along the sides, fuel tank cylinders between the axles, and cargo ribs with side panel textures.

Now I'm defining paint/material choices for cargo and cab panels using panelled and mottled textures, plus hazard stripe patterns, and setting up helper functions for placing boxes and parts before writing the final export.

Still building wheel geometry...

Adding brake disc and caliper details, then writing out the full wheel assembly code.
